import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

The runtime prompt.md is a template from a different project (FPS). Our actual user prompt is the Amazon 2D adventure game. We need to build it in this repo. No package.json currently. We can build a pure HTML5 canvas game with maybe a small build (no npm needed) served by default-start (html type → serve static). The `start.sh` requires `RUNTIME_DIR`, and project root served with index.html. Easiest: index.html + game JS/CSS static files, no package.json. Then `start.sh` works. Capture will screenshot. Design: A 2D side-scrolling / top-down adventure? Perhaps a top-down tile-based exploration with pixel art? Or a side-scrolling platformer? "Aventura 2D" could be like a top-down adventure (Zelda-like) with jungle, river, temples, puzzles, collectibles.

We have time to build a substantial game. Let's aim for a polished single-canvas game with:
- Canvas rendering at devicePixelRatio, responsive fit.
- Top-down explorer (boy/girl explorer) with walk animation, in a jungle with layered scenery, river, ruins.
- Stamina, health, machete to cut vegetation, torch to light dark temple, canoe to cross river, hidden glyph fragments, three medallions to open temple door, final lost city El Dorado reveal.
- Quest log / objectives in Spanish.
- Dialogue boxes with guide character (e.g., "Yara").
- Ambient particles (fireflies, leaves), parallax water, day/night gradient, sound (WebAudio synthesized ambient + sfx).
- Touch joystick + action button; keyboard WASD/arrows + E/Space.
- Title screen with button "Comenzar expedición".
- Save via localStorage? maybe not necessary but nice.
- Multiple zones: Jungle (camp), Riverbank (canoe), Ruins (temple), Lost City (final). Could implement all with a map system.

Given complexity, we can implement a tile-based world with several connected areas. However, huge scope risks bugs. Better: One cohesive hand-authored map scrollable with camera, containing jungle, river, ruins with three glyph pedestals, gate, and lost city beyond. Player explores; canoes auto-cross; collect 3 glyph stones from mini-challenges: 
1. Machete path to clear vines? A bush at north.
2. Glyph stone across the river via canoe.
3. Inside a dark cave/temple using torch, avoid? 

Maybe mini-puzzle: three stones hidden in different biomes. Collect to open the gate. Also a final "city" area beyond gate revealed with golden city, ending screen.

A single world of, say, 3200x2200 px with distinct regions. Camera follows player. Player walks with collision against water, cliffs, trees, ruins; can cross river on a bridge after repairing it (collect 2 logs?) Hmm.

Simplify yet rich: World as rooms/areas with transition rectangles, but single map easier for player. Let's do one large map horizontally:

- Middle: river crossing with canoe dock; need to find paddle? Could just press E at canoe to ride across animated.
- Right: temple ruins with 3 pedestals scattered around map.

Torch lighting can be a radial gradient overlay. Machete clear vines. Canoe crossing. Three abilities earned progressively:
1. Talk to Yara at camp → get machete + objective. Machete cuts vine blocking north path where "Piedra del Jaguar" sits in a small shrine.
2. At ruins, a dark temple doorway; need torch from camp. Yara gives torch after? Simplify: campfire grants torch when interacting (pick up torch).
3. Canoe: clicking E at canoe toggles river crossing; on other side ruins.
Maybe map layout: camp west (x 0-900), river vertical at x ~1000 (water band), ruins east x >1100, lost city gate at far east x ~2850. Cave in jungle south? 

Vertically bounded? Camera can show a nice large world. Let's build world 3000x1600. Player start (420, 900). Use simple cute pixel-ish vector character drawn via canvas shapes with walk bob and arm swing. Art style: lush painterly vector shapes, gradients, parallax, nice color palette. Could be very pretty with procedural foliage.

- Background: layered jungle floor gradient with texture noise (pre-rendered offscreen canvas for performance), paths, grass tufts, flowers, ferns, rocks, trees with shadows and highlights.
```js
export class AudioEngine {
  constructor(){ this.ctx=null; this.muted=false; this.master=null; }
  init(){ if(this.ctx) return; const AC=window.AudioContext||...; this.ctx=new AC(); this.master=this.ctx.createGain(); this.master.gain.value=0.55; this.master.connect(this.ctx.destination); this.startAmbient(); }
  setMuted(m){... ramp}
  startAmbient(){
    // brown-ish noise buffer 4s loop
    const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, ctx.sampleRate*4, ctx.sampleRate);
    data with filtered random;
    source loop -> biquad lowpass 520 -> gain 0.035 -> master
    // wind slow LFO on filter freq
    // insect chirp scheduler
    setInterval(...) if ctx state running
  }
  chirp(){ osc sine freq 2200→3200, gain env 0.02, 0.08s}
  footstep(){ noise burst 0.08s bandpass 300 }
  cut(){ noise burst 0.25 lowpass + osc 120 }
  pickup(){ three-note arpeggio triangle 660,880,1320 with envelopes}
  gate(){ low osc 55 -> 35, noise rumble 2s }
  splash()
  win(){ chord arpeggio }
  blip(){ short sine 700 }
}
```

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable 2D adventure game in Spanish set in the Amazon, where the player searches for the lost city of El Dorado.

## Requirements
- User request: "Un juego de aventura en 2d en el amazonas en busca de una cuidad perdida"
- Spanish UI and story.
- Playable on desktop and mobile with usable touch controls.
- Must render and be visually impressive in automated Playwright screenshots.

## Decisions
- Pure static HTML/CSS/JS site served by the existing `start.sh`/runtime static server, no npm build.
- Fully procedural canvas art and synthesized WebAudio; no external assets.
- Top-down adventure: camp → north jungle shrine → south torch-lit cave → canoe river crossing → ruins → three-glyph gate → golden lost city ending.
- Three sacred stones (jaguar, serpent, sun), machete for vines, torch for cave, canoe crossing, gate cutscene, ending stats.
- Keyboard: WASD/arrows, E/Space/Enter interact, Shift run, M mute. Touch: virtual joystick and action button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `css/style.css`, and all JS modules: `config.js`, `world.js`, `terrain.js`, `sprites.js`, `scenery.js`, `art.js`, `audio.js`, `game.js`.
- Implemented world generation, terrain, river, camp, shrine, cave, ruins, gate, city, props, collisions, interactions, dialogue, compass, HUD, particle/firefly systems, camera, cutscenes, ending, and debug API `window.__eldorado`.
- Syntax checks pass for all JS via `node --input-type=module --check`.
- Static server running in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Home/camp gameplay screenshot looks strong overall; title screen and gameplay render.

### Active
- Fixing visual and capture defects found in screenshots.
- Needs final desktop/mobile screenshot verification and possible visual polish.

### Blocked

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable 2D Amazon adventure game in Spanish where the player searches for the lost city of El Dorado.

## Requirements
- User request: "Un juego de aventura en 2d en el amazonas en busca de una cuidad perdida"
- Spanish UI and story.
- Playable on desktop and mobile with usable touch controls.
- Must render and be visually impressive in automated Playwright screenshots.

## Decisions
- Pure static HTML/CSS/JS site served by the existing `start.sh`/runtime static server, no npm build.
- Fully procedural canvas art and synthesized WebAudio; no external assets.
- Top-down adventure: camp → north jungle shrine → south torch-lit cave → canoe river crossing → ruins → three-glyph gate → golden lost city ending.
- Three sacred stones (jaguar, serpent, sun), machete for vines, torch for cave, canoe crossing, gate cutscene, ending stats.
- Keyboard: WASD/arrows, E/Space/Enter interact, Shift run, M mute. Touch: virtual joystick and action button.
- Title screen uses a frozen JPEG data-URL of the canvas as its backdrop; the live canvas is hidden (`display:none`) until gameplay starts to avoid compositor stalls during capture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `css/style.css`, and all JS modules: `config.js`, `world.js`, `terrain.js`, `sprites.js`, `scenery.js`, `art.js`, `audio.js`, `game.js`.
- Implemented world generation, terrain, river, camp, shrine, cave, ruins, gate, city, props, collisions, interactions, dialogue, compass, HUD, particles/fireflies, camera, cutscenes, ending, and debug API `window.__eldorado`.
- Fixed title clipping: `.title-inner` widened to 780px, title font reduced to `clamp(74px, 9.8vw, 140px)`; "EL DORADO" now renders fully.
- Removed title transform animations/start-button hover transforms; title animation is opacity-only; start button is geometrically stable.
- Fixed cave darkness: now only draws near/inside cave, soft elliptical gradient, full-screen inside cave, torch light clipped to cave walls; camp screenshot no longer has the near-black overlay blob.
- Fixed negative-width `rrect` in `config.js`; dock planks now render correctly instead of spiky artifacts.
- Expanded cave reserved area in `config.js` from `[80, 1250, 350, 470]` to `[20, 1220, 570, 560]`, removing trees/bushes from the cave interior.
- Reworked ground generation in `terrain.js` to slice the world into 512px tiles; `drawGround` in `game.js` draws visible tiles only.
- Added `willReadFrequently: true` to ground/tile 2D contexts; this eliminated the post-load compositor/rAF stall.
- Added `title-mode` class on `#app`; `#game` hidden during title and shown in `startGame()`/`replay()`.
- Painted and snapshotted title backdrop via `canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.9)` into `--title-art`; title looks lush and unclipped again.
- Auto-start capture now passes reliably 5/5 runs; idle rAF max gap reduced from ~3.2s to ~100ms.
- Verified title and camp visuals with screenshots; cave interior now clean; dock/canoe render correctly; shrine/ruins/gate/city render.
- Syntax checks pass for all JS via `node --input-type=module --check`.
- Static server running in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Verify final gameplay state transitions (canoe, gate, ending) using a fast-forward-aware flow test; renderer runs ~3fps under software GL so real-time cutscenes take ~7x longer than intended.
- Run the official `capture.sh` and inspect final desktop/mobile screenshots.
- Review mobile layout, touch controls, and dialogue states.

- `js/game.js`: main loop, player, interactions, cutscenes, UI, rendering, title backdrop snapshot, debug hooks.
